name: Support Desk
description: Answers questions from the administrators of the sites that upgrade from this one, from the documentation and FAQ for the release each site runs and, for a site joined to this management node, from what the site is doing now. Install it on a management node that serves sites.
author: System Developer

settings.name: support_desk_model
settings.label: Model that answers
settings.helptext: The model the support desk answers with, as your host or vendor names it. A support answer leaves this machine for the model's company, so this is normally a cloud model on your own key. Blank answers with whatever model with tools this node can reach.

settings.name: support_desk_system_prompt
settings.label: Voice of the support desk
settings.helptext: How the support desk speaks. Blank uses the shipped voice. The tool rules, the documentation map and the FAQ are always added after it and cannot be removed here.

settings.name: support_desk_daily_tokens_per_host
settings.label: Tokens one site may spend in a day
settings.helptext: Input and output tokens across every thread from one site in a UTC day. Over it, the site's panel says so and offers the documentation and a person. 0 means no per-site limit.

settings.name: support_desk_daily_tokens_total
settings.label: Tokens the support desk may spend in a day
settings.helptext: Input and output tokens across every site in a UTC day. 0 means no limit beyond Joinery AI's monthly cap.

settings.name: support_desk_new_threads_per_hour
settings.label: New threads accepted per hour from one address
settings.helptext: Questions that open a new thread, from one site or one visitor's address, counted when tried. Each one costs a call back to the site. Questions in an open thread, and the panel's polling, are not counted here: they carry the thread's token. Every container site on one host shares the host's address.

settings.name: support_desk_node_reads_per_thread
settings.label: Reads of a site per thread per day
settings.helptext: How many times in a UTC day one thread may ask a joined site's agent for something (a log, a report). 0 turns live reads off for every thread.

settings.name: support_desk_notify_email
settings.label: Email when a thread waits for a person
settings.helptext: One email when a thread asks for a person, naming the site, its version and the last message, at most one an hour for a thread. Empty sends none.

settings.name: support_desk_thread_retention_days
settings.label: Days to keep closed threads
settings.helptext: Closed threads older than this are deleted with their transcripts by the daily retention sweep. 0 keeps them: the threads, their thumbs and the answers people wrote are the record a better support desk is built from.

settings.name: support_desk_widget_enabled
settings.label: Answer visitors on the public pages
settings.helptext: Offers the support desk to visitors with no site yet, at /support_desk/ask, with a captcha on the first question and a per-address budget. They get the documentation of the newest release and the public pages; never a site's facts.

settings.name: support_desk_widget_daily_tokens_per_address
settings.label: Tokens one visitor address may spend in a day
settings.helptext: For the public widget only. 0 means no per-address limit.

settings.name: support_desk_system_user_id
settings.helptext: The reserved account that owns every support transcript, by user id. Made by the plugin's sync, disabled for sign-in; never a person.
